Morgan Stanley projects $MU gross margins could reach 90% in 2027 supported by 16 supply agreements with floor pricing and HBM sold out through 2027.

That contracted structure combined with a mix shift toward higher-margin HBM and data-center memory should structurally lift company-wide profitability while advanced packaging remains a huge chokepoint.

Also important to call out that HBM4 for $NVDA Vera Rubin platform began shipping in March 2026 and is ramping at roughly twice the pace of HBM3E 12-high scaling Micron’s highest-margin product into its strongest demand platform.

Data center capacity is projected to add ~106GW from 2026 through 2030 reaching 174GW and implying more than $5T of total spending.

That buildout could drive 50–60% of new U.S. power capacity through 2030 spanning $GEV turbines, $BE on-site fuel cells, $CEG and $VST generation and $VRT cooling and electrical infrastructure as hyperscalers work around years-long grid queues.

Once the power is secured, spending flows into $NVDA and $AMD accelerators, $AVGO and $MRVL custom silicon and networking, $TSM manufacturing and HBM from $MU, $SKHY and Samsung.

I also think as AI shifts toward more distributed and latency-sensitive inference in 2027 then demand should broaden beyond mega-campuses into edge and colocation facilities while $OKLO and $SMR offer longer-term nuclear optionality.

Its also important not to anchor your expectations to the portfolio’s most recent peak. 

You can buy $RKLB at $25, watch it climb to $150 and then feel devastated when it falls to $75 even though the position has still tripled from your original purchase price. 

I've seen a lot of members in my community treat that 50% decline as money that was taken away even though those gains were never realized and may have reflected a temporary level of excitement that the fundamentals hadn't yet earned (for this Rocket Lab example it was $SPCX IPO halo effect). 

If you measure every outcome from the highest price the stock ever reached then it will always create a distorted view of performance so someone who remains substantially ahead can begin behaving like an investor facing ruin simply because the portfolio statement no longer displays its peak value.

Something I've been community to the members is that the stock doesn't know where you bought it and the business isn't worth more simply because its shares traded higher a few months ago.. the decision should always be based on what the company is worth today and where the capital has the best opportunity to compound from here.

I do recommend hedging a portfolio with this level of risk but this drawdown has been especially difficult because my rule is to add hedges only when $QQQ breaks below its 21-week EMA.

The indices have held up while rolling bear markets hit different sectors so my hedge trigger never activated and the portfolio absorbed the full drawdown.

I’m also incredibly proud of how much my 5K+ member community has grown and matured over the years.

This is the 6th time the portfolio has pulled back 10% or more in the past three years on its way to nearly 4x but during this drawdown I’ve noticed a clear shift in confidence and discipline around using market weakness to add to the strongest companies shaping the new economy.

I’m currently experiencing my worst monthly portfolio performance since 2023.

Whats even more wild to me is the number of bears beating their chests during this drawdown.. especially because the portfolios being hit hardest are likely the same ones that dramatically outperformed the market over the past several years.

That doesn't make losing money any easier but its an important reminder that the volatility hurting those positions today is inseparable from the volatility that produced the earlier gains (even after drawdown my portfolio is still compounding at 73% CAGR).

I also value periods like this because they give me the opportunity to rebuild the portfolio around the companies and themes I want to own most once the market moves beyond this digestion phase.

The long-term AI buildout isn't stopping but not every company will emerge stronger since the real work is identifying which businesses are experiencing temporary price pressure and which are showing genuine deterioration then positioning the portfolio around the companies whose moats continue strengthening through the drawdown.

The same concentration that creates exceptional years will occasionally create brutal months where the goal isn't to avoid volatility altogether but to make sure the portfolio is built around businesses capable of compounding through it and to use the dislocation to improve our positioning for the next phase of the cycle.

$SPCX Starmind AI satellites could route data through Starlink’s laser mesh avoiding complex onboard antennas and most direct spectrum requirements.

That lets Starmind piggyback on more than 10,000 Starlink satellites with V3 models potentially carrying 2–3 Tbps each. 

This creates a distribution moat no standalone orbital-compute player can match but it also shifts the bottleneck to the ground by funneling enormous traffic through SpaceX’s gateways.

Which is why SpaceX is expanding into E-, V- and W-band backhaul with D-band proposed for AI while new FCC rules replacing 1990s power limits could unlock up to 7x more capacity from the same satellite network.
